title: The escape trip
old_caption: Booked a flight to outrun the feelings? They pack themselves. Tonight, walk the block with a friend, and plan the trip later for joy.

title: Working through it
old_caption: Fourteen-hour days can feel like coping, but busy isn't the same as better. Log off, give the feelings ten minutes, and let rest count as healing.

title: “We're still friends!”
old_caption: Trying to be friends with your ex on day one? Space first isn't cold, it's kind. A friendship can come later, once it doesn't hurt.

title: Crying at everything
old_caption: Cried at a drawing of a dog? Tears are your heart doing the work. Drink some water, eat something, sleep. Send this to your friend who's crying at everything this week.

title: The emergency floor visit
old_caption: You don't need a speech when you're hurting, you need company. Let your friends in, even if the kitchen is a mess and you're lying on the floor.

title: The bad day on day 23
old_caption: One song and it feels like day one again. A bad day isn't starting over: healing goes up and down, and every day you've done still counts.

title: The first good morning
old_caption: The first morning they aren't your first thought feels strange, then quiet, then good. Healing isn't a parade. Notice it, and make a plan.

title: Libra: 30 days in 60 seconds
old_caption: A whole month of healing in one minute: the bad days, the friend with the blanket, the party you left early, the first good morning. Let the bad days be bad, and let one friend in.

title: Scorpio: the situationship, 30 days
old_caption: It was never official and it still hurts. That's allowed. Thirty days of muting, almost-texting and finally saying it out loud, because untitled still counts.

title: Aquarius: 30 days of feelings, logged
old_caption: You can't debug a feeling, you have to feel it. Thirty days from "not responding" to the patch notes, with one friend who drags you outside to look up.
